node.title: Algorithms & Mistakes by Wimer Hazenberg (aka Monokai) @A-Lab
node.description:
Hello again **creative coders** and **enthusiasts**!

**Thank you** to everyone that showed up for the social in the park last month. We had a great time! As we were just about lucky enough to stay dry then, this month we're heading back indoors. And not just anywhere!

We're very happy and excited to announce that we're welcomed at **[A-Lab](https://www.a-lab.nl/)** for our **August** meetup. A-Lab is situated just across the water from Central Station and with their tagline "**Where Curious Works**" we just had to get in touch. Turns out they're amazing people doing cool stuff and they're happy to have us. We are very grateful for this budding partnership and look forward to grow and nurture it as we go.

But enough about logistics, as we've got more to be excited about! For August we've got another great speaker lined up for you all!

On **August 21st** **[Wimer Hazenberg](https://wimer.frl/)** aka **[Monokai](https://monokai.com/)** will be joining us at A-Lab for a talk titled "Algorithms & Mistakes".

If you've been anywhere near a code editor in last 20 years, you most probably saw the *arguably coolest* color scheme '**Monokai**' pass by, which was created by Wimer back in 2006. Since then he's built [awwwardwinning sites](https://minimalwim.com/), created stunning '[fog-photography](https://monokai.com/work/environmental-operations)' and most recently has been focusing on [Algorithmic Art](https://monokai.com/work/overview). Which is also the focus of his talk.

🗣️ **Wimer Hazenberg: Algorithms & Mistakes**
At the core of algorithmic art lies the **randomizer**. Over-regulate it, and the results become predictable. Let it run free, and chaos takes over. This talk explores how embracing unexpected outcomes can lead to surprising and inspiring creative discoveries.

After the talk, we'll be opening up the floor to admire the results of our very first [Space Invaders themed coding challenge](https://cca.codes/invaders). Make sure to enter your entry **before** **August 18th**.

We're looking forward to seeing you there!

⚠️⚠️⚠️**Important Logistical Note** ⚠️⚠️⚠️
**[SAIL 2025](https://www.sail.nl/)** is on during our next meetup, which means there's **a lot** of **people and boats** around Central Station. According to the [GVB ](https://www.gvb.nl/sail)all ferry's to get to A-Lab will be operational, though there might be **extra waiting time**. Please make sure to account for this as good as possible. Thank you!
⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️⚠️

node.title: Sunday Social @ Vondelpark
node.description:
Hello again **everyone**!

Last month we were welcomed at **[Multitude](https://www.multitude.nl/)**[ ](https://www.multitude.nl/)at their cosy office where we had a great time. We want to **thank** them for being great hosts and supporting the open source community.

But as the **summer** seems to have arrived, it is that time of year again where we can leave our buzzing laptops and beamers for what they are and head into green and sunny\* **outdoors**. And what better place than the **Vondelpark**?

We'll be meeting in the park on **Sunday 13th** of July at **13:30.**

This time around we'd like to invite everybody to bring along a **game** that can be **played** together in the **park**. That could be a deck of **cards**, or a **frisbee**. Or maybe something completely different. Or you can just come and **hang out**. That's also totally cool.

We'll also bring a **cooler** box, some ice and some drinks, but feel free to bring along what you like.

Find us around here:
[https://www.google.com/maps/place/52%C2%B021'27.0%22N+4%C2%B052'01.2%22E/@52.3575085,4.8644147,17z/](https://www.google.com/maps/place/52%C2%B021'27.0%22N+4%C2%B052'01.2%22E/@52.3575085,4.8644147,17z/)

Hope to see you all there!
And/or online, on our **[Discord](https://discord.gg/qrrKkaM4w3)**

node.title: Tools Special @Multitude
node.description:
Hello again creative coding enthusiasts!

While we're still **buzzing** from last edition, we've already got the next one ready for you, all hot and fresh.

This time around we'll be crossing the water and head into **Noord** where we're invited over at the creative agency **[Multitude](https://www.multitude.nl/)**. We're looking forward to exploring yet another new corner of the city, but what we're really excited about this time around is what we'll be talking about there.

**[Aidan Wyber](https://aidanwyber.com/)**, who is officially *the* creative coder over at Multitude, will be introducing the brand new **open-source creative tool** **p5Brandlab**, built with p5js and on top of all the hard earned brand-building experience Aidan gained working real-world client projects at Multitude.

p5Brandlab is an open-source framework for fellow creative coders to create visual & dynamic **brand identities**. And this all wrapped up in a neat and tidy client-proof UI. We're very excited to see what you all can make with it!

After the presentation, we'll be opening up the floor for a good old fashion themed **show-and-tell**. The theme? You've guessed it! **Tools**!! The theme is more of a possible inspriation source rather than a guideline, so please don't be shy! :)

Hope to see you there!
Or online on our **[Discord](https://discord.gg/qrrKkaM4w3)**

node.title: May Madness @Mollie
node.description:
As usual, we'd like to **thank** everyone who joined us for the **Plotter Special** last month! Seeing everybody huddled around the plotters was really something...

This month **May**, as we're invited back at our friends at **Mollie**'s we tried to make it even **Madder**.

Which is why, we've got not 1, not 2, but **3 amazing speakers** for you this time around!

In alphabetical order, we start off with **Giedrius Tamulaitis**, who's bringing along a peculiarly **doomed** rotary **phone**.

Continuing in alphabetical order, we've got **Masa**, who will take us on a tour through the **interactive pixel-art** wonder worlds he creates.

And finally, last but not least, still in alphabetical order, we are welcoming **Piter Pasma** to the stage. He's going to tell us a bit about his work on his "**Rayhatcher**" algorithm and the use, **beauty** and **magic** of **SDFs**.

Are you excited? Because we sure are!
We hope to see you there! Or if you can't make it, come hang out on **[our Discord](https://discord.gg/qrrKkaM4w3)**.

⚠️ As we've got a packed and exciting program we kindly ask you to try to be **punctual** so we can get an early start.

**📅 Program Details:**

**☎️ Doom Phone** \- Coder and artist **[Giedrius Tamulaitis](https://tamulaitis.lt/)** will tell us a story about turning an old rotary phone into a wireless controller that can be used to play Doom. For no good reason. And you will be able to try it out!

🐰 **Interactive Pixel Art -** Creative Coder **[Masa](https://ma5a.com/)**[ ](https://ma5a.com/)used to draw things like bunnies pretending to be an ice cream, and these days he codes things like dancing meerkats. He will be telling the story of how he started creative coding and share some of his work and the processes behind them.

**☀️ Rayhatcher / SDFs - [Piter Pasma](https://piterpasma.nl/)** is a generative artist from Groningen, the Netherlands, who creates three-dimensional artworks using compact mathematical code. Known for his "[Rayhatcher](https://fxwho.xyz/fxhash/urh/)" algorithm—line-art-inspired raymarching optimized for plotters. Pasma also fosters creative coding communities through initiatives like [Genuary ](https://genuary.art/)and the collaborative Universal Rayhatcher project. In his presentation he will talk about his "Rayhatcher" algorithm and the use, beauty and magic of SDFs.

**🔗 Links:**

* Doom phone: https://tamulaitis.lt/project/dialrhea/
* Giedrius's tech & art projects: https://tamulaitis.lt/
* Masa's website: https://ma5a.com/
* Masa's projects on Codepen: https://codepen.io/Ma5
* Piter's website: https://piterpasma.nl/
* Genuary: https://genuary.art/
* Skulptuur Gallery: https://skulpturen.nl/
* Universal Rayhatcher: https://fxwho.xyz/fxhash/urh/

node.title: Plotter Special @Miro
node.description:
**Check the comment for the instructions how to find us in the Miro office!**

Hello again creative coders and enthusiasts!

**Thank you** to those who joined us for our fun and inspiring poetry themed afternoon at CREA last month. While we were just getting comfortable in our cosy corner there, this time around we're going somewhere else.

For our April edition we are invited back to our friends over at **Miro**'s. Well, same friends but a different location as they moved offices last month. We're excited to see where they landed.

What we're even more excited about though, is this month's topic: **Pen Plotters**! A topic near and dear to us. For those unfamiliar with the term, a 'pen plotter' is a device that holds a pen and can do X, Y, pen up & pen down movement. They come in different shapes and sizes and can also hold more than just a pen. People get very creative with them and even build their own contraptions...

In our upcoming special we'll give a brief overview of the **history** of plotters and a selection of **artists we love**, and share some of our own plotter work. However this is also an invitation to you to **share** what you've seen or made in the space that got you all excited. Anything goes!

To top it all off, there's even more! David and Stanko will be bringing along their **AxiDraw's** (A3) and we'll be doing some **plotting on the spot**! If you've always wanted to try and plot something but never got around to it, this could be your chance!

We've made an **[upload form](https://forms.cca.codes/svg)**[ ](https://forms.cca.codes/svg)where you can drop your **SVG**s. As plotting takes time and our time is limited, we might have to make a selection of what exactly we can plot, but don't let that stop you! We're happy to provide **advice** or **feedback**, just drop a note with the upload and we'll get back to you.

Or come and ask your question on **[our Discord](https://discord.gg/qrrKkaM4w3)!**

For now we'll end with these few resources, The first is an informative **article** about pen plotting and its history:
**[How Pen Plotting Evolved into a Form of Art - Jared MapleThorpe](https://penplotter.art/p/pen-plotter-art-history)**
The second is for if you want to get started but don't know how, this page has a bunch of **SVG generators** to jump right in:
**[SVG Tools by DrawingBots (Maks Surguy)](https://drawingbots.net/knowledge/tools)**
Or if you want to **dive deeper** and generate the SVGs yourself, there's a bunch **more resources** here:
**[How to Pen Plot - Admin :)](https://penplotterartwork.com/blog/2021/07/05/how-to-pen-plot-guides-tutorials-and-more/)**

Or you can use one of the **[tools](https://neon.muffinman.io/)**[ ](https://neon.muffinman.io/)made by **[David](https://rstr.d17e.dev)** or **[Stanko](https://muffinman.io/vertigo/)** for this very purpose :)

node.title: Poetry Afternoon @ CREA
node.description:
This time we planned something a little bit different: a **Poetry Afternoon**!

It is going to be a **working session** where we gather to **create** some **digital/machine/robot** **poetry**.

**What is this digital poetry?** You can create an actual poem, or invent a new language, generate an image that resembles a poem, or even a karaoke machine. Feel free to interpret it as you like! It doesn't have to be done by code at all. If you know any poetry nerds, please bring them along!

One little thing, we would prefer if you avoid using LLMs. It is not about asking AI for an amazing poem, but rather about having fun creating and exploring. However, feel free to use AI if you need help with coding.

Some **text** **sources** you can use:

* [Project Gutenberg](https://www.gutenberg.org/)
* [Standard EBooks](https://standardebooks.org/)
* [The CMU Pronouncing Dictionary](https://github.com/Alexir/CMUdict/blob/master/cmudict-0.7b) \- A dictionary of English words and their pronunciations\, which can be used to generate rhymes\.

For **inspiration**, you can check out the following videos:

* [Making machine poetry with train wagons and OC](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RESKH-XAv0s)
* [Comedy Writing With Small Generative Models](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M2o4f_2L0No)

We're looking forward to seeing you there, or if you can't make it, come say hi on our [Discord](https://discord.gg/qrrKkaM4w3)

node.title: After Work Session @VolksHotel
node.description:
**February** has seemingly just begun, yet its end is already in sight. But fear not, we have another gathering planned before that end is nigh!

We had an amazing time at the Genuary edition, so we'll be following a similar format: a combination of **sharing projects** and a **social event**. Though this time we'll be visiting our friends over at **VolksHotel** again for that great mix of work and leisure.

You can bring your **laptop** or **tablet** to share your work, or just come hang out and have a **chat**!

No theme this time around, as we've been planning some more elaborate and exciting sessions for the months to come, but more on that very soon...

We're looking forward to seeing you there, or if you can't make it, come say hi on our [Discord](https://discord.gg/qrrKkaM4w3)

node.title: Genuary Special @ CREA Cafe
node.description:
Hello again **creative coders** and enthusiasts!

We hope you all had warm and joyful **holidays** while the weather has been anything but. Luckily, it is also a time with plenty of reasons to stay indoors.

One of those reasons that has been keeping us warm and busy in **2025** so far, is **[Genuary](https://genuary.art)**. For those unfamiliar, genuary is 'an artificially generated month of time where we build code that makes beautiful things'. Or 31 prompts, one for each day of **January**, meant to inspire and tickle your creative coding itch.

So that is why, for our next meetup we'll have **'Genuary'** as the **theme**, while as format we're mixing things up a little bit again.

This time we're having a **mix** of a **social event** and a **group-work session**. There will be space for laptops, so you can get some work done (right in time before Genuary ends :) or show off your creations or something you've seen online... Bringing a laptop is totally optional though. So if you just want to hang out for a chat and see what everyone's up to that's perfectly cool as well.

We've reserved the long tables next to the bar in **CREA Cafe**, to accomodate our format and we'll also make sure there's **wifi** available this time around.

**Hope to see you all there!**

node.title: Social @ Troost, de Pijp
node.description:
As the year comes to an end we want to wrap it up with a relaxed **social** event.

No presentations, laptops or beamers, *just* a bunch of fun and interesting **people getting together** for a chat an a drink.

We'll be meeting on **Wednesday 18th** of **December** at the **Brouwerij Troost**, **de Pijp**.

Even though this time around there's no agenda's nor themes, we'd love to see you there and **hear** all about how the last year was for you and what you'd like to see for **2025**. Be it about personal plans, the world, or from these meetups...

It's now almost been a year that we've been organizing these and we want to take this time to collect some **feedback** from you and discuss some of the ideas we have for he future.

So we’d **love** to see you there!

If you can’t make it this time, we still want to hear your thoughts and ideas!
That’s why we prepared [this little form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSegmjMWkxoHs5BZNkybD43oFaKFioJfcRhUIzWobUXaiKojXA/viewform).
It would be really great if you filled it out and help us shape how next year looks like for CCA.
I mean… If you’ve read this far, I’d say you care at least a little bit how that’ll look like, right? Well, here’s your chance… we promise we will listen!

And we’re still looking for a better banner! Hit us up over on [our discord](https://discord.gg/qrrKkaM4w3)

node.title: Sunday Session @ CREA Café
node.description:
Hello again creative coders and enthusiasts!

Last month we had an epic event in collaboration with **[Dance Hack](https://www.dancehack.nl/)** over at **[Splendor](https://splendoramsterdam.com/)**. We want to thank the dance hack crew for co-hosting and especially everyone that showed up and joined us for the workshop. It was a bit chaotic, but fun and engaging for everyone there. **Thank you all!**

Now for this time around, we're going back to an improved **CREA Cafe** setting where we've got something planned we've done before, yet a little bit different. We'll be doing a **flash-talk on Hydra**, the visual live coding environment, followed-up with a **themed show and tell**.

🕰️ **Schedule**
**13:00** \- Start & welcome
**13:30** \- Hydra Crash Course by David Vandenbogaerde
**14:00** \- Themed show & tell\, theme: Synthesizers

🗣️ **Crash Course Hydra** by **David Vandenbogaerde**

**Hydra** is a browser-based platform for live coding visuals developed by **Olivia Jack**. The API is inspired by analog modular **synthesis**, in which multiple visual sources (oscillators, cameras, application windows, other connected windows) can be transformed, modulated, and composited via combining sequences of functions.

**David** has been developing software for about twenty years now and as the co-organizer of the CCA meetups, it should come to no surprise to you that he likes his coding creative. So when he finally sat down to play around with **Hydra** in a workshop at **C3** earlier this year, it really got under his skin. In this flash talk he'll take you through all the things Hydra he's learned in the mean time, and who knows, maybe pass on the Hydra bug.

🙉 **Themed Show & Tell**

The theme for this meetup is: **Synthesizers**.
As Hydra was inspired by analog synthesizers, we thought that was the perfect opportunity to have that as the theme. And please **interpret as broadly as you like**!

**Anyone** can share a project or thoughts on the topic. This can either be something you did, or something you found interesting. Whatever the topic brings up in you, we'd love to hear and see it!

As for the location, we're heading back to our corner spot at **CREA Cafe**, only this time we'll be bringing an actual screen on top of the projector. And some curtains probably to make the '**living room**' a bit cosier.

**Hope to see you there!**

Or online, on our Discord
